text.arabic_uthmani: ۞ قَالُوٓا۟ إِن يَسْرِقْ فَقَدْ سَرَقَ أَخٌۭ لَّهُۥ مِن قَبْلُ ۚ فَأَسَرَّهَا يُوسُفُ فِى نَفْسِهِۦ وَلَمْ يُبْدِهَا لَهُمْ ۚ قَالَ أَنتُمْ شَرٌّۭ مَّكَانًۭا ۖ وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا تَصِفُونَ

words.gloss_range: reported collective saying that launches the brothers' conditional accusation as accountable speech
words.root_gloss_range: speech, saying, claiming, and verbal response; locally the plural perfect opens an attributed group claim
words.prose: {{ar:قَالُوا}} ({{tr:qālū}}) opens the ayah as group speech. The plural form keeps the brothers unnamed as a collective, while the quoted conditional stays inside their accountable claim rather than narrator-certified fact. The same speech root later returns in Joseph's singular reply, so the scene is framed as many accusers answered by one restrained speaker; in this opening, brotherhood is already mediated by hostile speech rather than simple kinship. Echoes with earlier deception speech (12:18), the oath scene (12:73), and the later refusal (12:79) keep this utterance inside Surah 12's speech-conflict chain, and the shared long qāl sound lets recitation hear the parallel before the plural-singular contrast is parsed.

words.gloss_range: conditional opening that makes the present theft claim formally hypothetical while enabling an accusatory inference
words.prose: {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) keeps the present theft claim formally conditional. That openness is strategic: the brothers do not grammatically convict Benjamin in the first clause, but they immediately steer the condition toward a hardened past precedent. The particle therefore makes the accusation sound cautious while preparing the reader for the certainty marker that follows, and its nasal close flows into the theft verb it governs.

words.gloss_range: conditional jussive theft allegation with no named object; covert taking is alleged but not grammatically certified as fact
words.root_gloss_range: stealing and covert taking; locally a dependent imperfect makes theft a conditional scenario rather than a settled report
words.prose: {{ar:يَسْرِقْ}} ({{tr:yasriq}}) is a dependent jussive, so the alleged theft remains inside the condition; the clipped final stop is the audible trace of that dependency. Its object is unstated, which lets suspicion spread without naming what was taken. The s-r-q field still gives the accusation covert-taking force, and the same rare root returns in the next verb, letting the brothers slide from possible present conduct into an alleged completed past while the theft sound carries toward Joseph's later concealment.

Bound to the next particle, it compresses sequence and certainty, making the inference feel immediate: if this happens, then the family precedent is already ready.

words.gloss_range: completed past theft claim with unstated object; active agency is local, while variant pressure keeps attribution contested
words.root_gloss_range: stealing and covert taking; locally the perfect verb makes an alleged past act function as precedent
words.prose: {{ar:سَرَقَ}} ({{tr:saraqa}}) supplies the alleged completed theft. Its object remains unstated, so the past event functions more like stigma than documentation. The standard active form assigns agency to the later brother-noun, while the passive-variant pressure keeps the reader aware that attribution itself is contested. Locally, the brothers use the rare theft root to redirect shame from their own denial of theft (12:73) toward Joseph's line, converting a possible present accusation into a supposed family pattern whose s-r-q sound is answered by later s-r-r concealment.

words.gloss_range: indefinite brother-agent linked to Benjamin, leaving Joseph implied rather than named
words.root_gloss_range: brotherhood, kinship, and close relation; locally the possessive phrase favors sibling relation and carries blame by kinship
words.prose: {{ar:أَخٌ}} ({{tr:akhun}}) names the alleged agent only as an indefinite brother. That gives the accusation force while avoiding Joseph's name, even though Joseph is present and will be named as the concealing subject. The possessive phrase narrows the relation toward Benjamin's brother, but the indefinite form lets blame travel through kinship rather than through direct evidence. The irony deepens across the surah: private brotherly reassurance (12:69) is inverted into public brotherly accusation here, and Joseph later names what was done to him and his brother (12:89).

The delayed phrase narrows the indefinite noun after it has already sounded open, and the later plural pronoun phrase reverses the same lām-pronoun shape from possession into withheld disclosure.

words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) opens the past as a source. Here the source is temporal rather than spatial: suspicion is made to come from before. Its delayed phrase closes the brothers' statement, so prior time becomes the final evidentiary pressure in their accusation, and the nasal particle binds audibly to the following time word as one temporal unit.

words.gloss_range: compressed prior-time adverb that closes the accusation with an unstated before-this complement
words.root_gloss_range: before, facing, receiving, or prior orientation; locally the preposition selects temporal precedence
words.prose: {{ar:قَبْلُ}} ({{tr:qablu}}) closes the brothers' charge with compressed prior time. The form carries a suppressed complement, so the listener supplies before this moment. Its q-b-l field can face other branches, but the phrase selects temporal precedence: the brothers turn before into precedent, a fronted past made to stand in front of Benjamin as proof. That same phrase contrasts later with true retrospective fulfillment (12:100) and earlier with Jacob's memory of trust (12:64).

words.gloss_range: narrative connector that pivots from public accusation to Joseph's inward response
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) returns the ayah from the brothers' quotation to narrative action. Bound to the concealment verb, it makes Joseph's concealment the immediate sequel to their accusation without making it part of their speech. The small connector is therefore the hinge from public claim to private interiority, carrying the scene from external accusation into Joseph's inward world.

words.gloss_range: deliberate concealment of an inferred feminine object, locally the spoken matter or response held inward
words.root_gloss_range: secrecy, concealing, and also gladness in the wider family; local Form IV with inner-location phrase selects active concealment
words.prose: {{ar:أَسَرَّهَا}} ({{tr:asarrahā}}) makes concealment the center of the ayah. The feminine suffix forces the reader to infer the hidden object, most naturally the spoken matter or response generated by the accusation, while the variant with masculine suffix would shift that hidden object toward a more general matter. Form IV makes the concealment deliberate, and the inner-location phrase selects secrecy rather than gladness as the local sense, though the root family still lets the hidden matter feel inwardly held. The word reverses an earlier concealment scene: Joseph was hidden as merchandise (12:19), but here Joseph controls what remains hidden; its doubled rāʾ and s-r onset turn the theft sound into tightened inward secrecy.

words.prose: {{ar:يُوسُفُ}} ({{tr:yūsufu}}) names Joseph after the concealment verb. That naming fixes him as the conscious agent of restraint and also destabilizes the brothers' indirect accusation, because the implied prior brother is standing in the scene as the named judge. The name sits at the pivot between their hostile speech and his inner control, and its softer rounded cadence marks a calm center between the compressed concealment verb and the inner-self phrase.

Spatial grammar becomes psychological interiority: Joseph does not answer by outward disclosure first; the matter is placed inside. The inner-self phrase is completed before the negated reveal clause, so the ayah first lets the preposition and self noun flow as one contained unit, then shows denied outward release.

words.prose: {{ar:نَفْسِهِ}} ({{tr:nafsihi}}) makes Joseph's own self the hidden chamber of the scene. The suffix binds that interior to him specifically, and the singular noun keeps the response in one private locus rather than in public speech. The root's breath pressure fits the restraint: the n-f-s texture makes the response feel held inward as something not released. Across Surah 12, self-language can name embellished plotting (12:18, 12:83), hidden desire (12:51), or controlled interiority here, and the closing divine knowledge clause covers precisely such hidden contents.

It governs the following jussive reveal verb, so Joseph did not merely postpone disclosure; in that scene, he did not reveal the matter to them. The particle turns hidden knowledge into controlled practice, with its effect visible across the word boundary in the form of the reveal verb.

words.root_gloss_range: supplied b-d-d evidence overlaps a classical disclose or appear field; locally the Form IV verb means to make the hidden matter manifest
words.prose: {{ar:يُبْدِهَا}} ({{tr:yubdihā}}) is the reveal side of the conceal-reveal pair, but it appears under negation. The same feminine object suffix carries the hidden matter from Joseph's inward concealment into the blocked act of manifestation, so the final -hā remains audible even while disclosure is denied. The supplied root assignment is tense with the classical disclose or appear field, so recurrence claims must be cautious; locally, the sense is clear: Joseph does not cause the matter to appear to them. Echoes with conceal/reveal knowledge formulas (3:154; 2:33) make the restraint more than silence; it is an epistemic act.

words.prose: {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) brings Joseph's singular saying after the non-disclosure clause. Because he did not reveal the hidden matter to them, the boundary of this saying remains tense: it may be outward reply or inward continuation. Either way, the plural opening verb has narrowed to one speaker, and the shared qāl core lets sound mark the speaker shift before the speech act reverses the brothers' accusation by judging their position worse.

words.root_gloss_range: bad, worse, and moral deficiency; supplied sh-r-y evidence also recalls sale, but local syntax selects comparative judgment
words.prose: {{ar:شَرٌّ}} ({{tr:sharrun}}) reverses the moral direction of the brothers' accusation. Joseph does not merely say they are wrong; the elative makes them worse in the domain the next word specifies. The supplied sh-r-y root assignment narrows into an ironic undertone rather than replacing the local evil or worse sense: those associated with selling Joseph (12:20) are now judged through a word that the data links to sale, while the grammar selects comparative moral ranking. The formula also resonates with a marked condemnation register (5:60), and the doubled rāʾ makes the counter-judgment acoustically heavy.

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the final divine-knowledge clause. It can resume beyond Joseph's retort, so the ayah does not end with human counter-judgment alone. Fused to the divine name, the connector gives the closure a clean launch and lets the discourse rise from accusation and response into the epistemic register that also closed the previous ayah.

words.root_gloss_range: divine name field tied to worship and ultimate authority; locally it names the subject who knows beyond human descriptions
words.prose: {{ar:اللَّهُ}} ({{tr:allāhu}}) names the subject of the closing knowledge clause. The authority over what the brothers describe is not anonymous; the divine name stands over both their accusation and Joseph's counter-judgment, and it qualifies even human moral speech by placing it under God's knowledge. The clause also answers the prior ayah's hierarchy of knowledge (12:76) by naming the apex that was left implicit, while the doubled lām gives the seal audible weight.

words.gloss_range: absolute elative predicate of divine knowledge, with no explicit comparator needed
words.root_gloss_range: knowing, knowledge, teaching, and informing; locally the elative marks God as knowing best
words.prose: {{ar:أَعْلَمُ}} ({{tr:aʿlamu}}) is the semantic center of the closure. As an elative without an explicit than-phrase, it functions as knowing best rather than a limited comparison. The form places the brothers' descriptions, and even human counter-speech, beneath divine knowledge; God knows not only facts but the quality of their describing. It also converts the knowledge hierarchy of the previous ayah (12:76) into a named divine superlative and anticipates Jacob's later knowledge claim (12:96).

topics.reason: Rows link aʿlamu to the following description complement and to 12:76, 12:86, and 12:96 knowledge scenes.

words.gloss_range: specifying preposition that gives divine knowledge its governed domain: what they describe
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) gives the knowledge predicate its domain. In the following prepositional-relative phrase, it means concerning or with respect to, not instrument, and it draws the whole relative description clause under divine knowledge. The closure is therefore targeted rather than abstract: God knows best about the content and quality of what they describe, with the recited bi-mā liaison making that complement sound like one governed gateway.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun that nominalizes the open-ended content of their description
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) turns the brothers' describing into a knowable what. Governed by the preceding preposition, it is relative rather than interrogative or negative. Because it does not specify the content narrowly, the divine audit can gather the accusation, its motives, and the broader characterization they are making; all their attribution is compressed into one recoverable content domain.

topics.reason: The preceding preposition and following verb route mā as a relative pronoun.

words.gloss_range: second-person plural description or attribution under divine audit; supplied root tension is narrowed to local describing sense
words.root_gloss_range: supplied ṣ-f-f root data is tense with the local description field; locally the verb is describing or ascribing, not arranging rows
words.prose: {{ar:تَصِفُونَ}} ({{tr:taṣifūna}}) is the ayah's final surface action: not theft, but describing or attributing. The second-person plural ending keeps the brothers under direct audit, and the open object lets God's knowledge cover whatever they are characterizing. The supplied root data is tense with row-ordering, so the local sense must be narrowed to description/ascription; that narrowing matters because the verse closes by judging the quality and accuracy of their constructed portrayal. The final verb reaches back to the opening speech verb, reclassifying speech as characterization under divine knowledge, and the phrase echoes Jacob's earlier response to their false account (12:18) and the wider warning about lying description (16:116). The closing ṣ/f friction carries the judgment from the moral judgment into the last word.

topics.reason: The imperfect 2mp form makes the brothers the direct subject and leaves the content open through the relative construction.

topics.headline: description despite supplied root tension

topics.reason: The local phrase requires describe/ascribe; the supplied ṣ-f-f tension is retained only as a caution for root-based recurrence.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The doubled theft language, its transfer through "a brother of his," and the closing "what you describe."
baseline_models.mechanism: The brothers move from a conditional present allegation to a past allegation attached through kinship. The theft root itself carries a branch for attributing theft to a person, while saying and describing externalize that attribution. The focus therefore keeps two readings live: a report about acts and a social act that fixes a theft-identity onto people without itself settling the truth of either report.

activation_trace.role: Literally names the attribution of theft to a person; here it makes the repeated verbs operate as labels as well as alleged acts.
Literally covers saying or assigning what was not said or was not so; here it keeps the brothers' spoken assignment epistemically contestable.
Literally renders a thing by its stated features; here it classifies the accusation as an outward representation rather than transparent knowledge.

changed_reading.before: The brothers report that the present brother steals because his brother stole before.
changed_reading.after: The verse also stages accusation as a second kind of taking: speech captures a person's standing by attaching a theft-description across kinship and time.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: "He concealed it within himself and did not disclose it to them; he said..."
baseline_models.mechanism: Concealment, self, non-disclosure, and saying form a private speech channel. The counter-judgment can be semantically complete while socially unavailable: narration gives the reader access to speech that the brothers do not receive. This preserves the live grammatical question of whether the final "he said" is wholly inward or partly outward while rejecting a simple equation of saying with audible disclosure.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: "A brother of his before" is answered by the plural "you are worse in place."
baseline_models.mechanism: The brothers route liability through brotherhood and temporal precedence. Kinship can transmit an accusation in their model, while the answer relocates comparison to the speakers' current stance and leaves definitive knowledge with God.

context_deltas.mechanism: The brothers immediately place a favorable description of Joseph beside a request to arrest one person in another's place. Joseph answers by restricting seizure to the person with whom the goods were found and calls the alternative a wrong placement. This operationalizes the focus's contrast between description and knowledge: praise may be sincere, strategic, or both, but it cannot authorize moving liability to a substitute body.

context_deltas.mechanism: The exact self-root moves from Joseph's singular interior, where a judgment is contained, to the brothers' plural selves, which are said to have adorned or facilitated an affair. Interiority is therefore not automatically truthful or deceptive: it can restrain a harmful disclosure, or it can manufacture a compelling account. Beautiful patience supplies a third operation, holding the self without endorsing its narration.

This reenacts the focus's gap between what observers describe and what another knows, while showing that containment can route speech and action rather than terminate them.

strongest_changes: The inherited theft claim becomes an inspectable act of attribution, then is bounded by finding, witness, unseen limits, and corroboration.
Joseph's inward sentence becomes an audience-and-timing mechanism that later turns into a recognition-producing question and explicit non-reproach.
Brotherhood changes from the conduit of stigma in "a brother of his" to the reclaimed first-person bond "this is my brother," followed by the accusers' self-confession.
The repeated self-root keeps opposed inner mechanisms live: restrained truth, an adorned account, patient containment, selective disclosure, and renewed search.
summary.what_was_special: The window repeatedly reactivates the focus's exact contrasts: place versus substitution, description versus knowledge, hidden speech versus selected disclosure, and brotherhood as stigma versus solidarity. The split ش ر ي exchange target, covert-listening theft branch, and breath-pressure sequence add contained cross-domain readings that a conservative synthesis would likely lose.
remaining_uncertainties: The precise referent of the feminine object in "he concealed it" and whether the following "he said" is wholly inward or partly audible remain grammatically live.
The brothers' praise, evidentiary caveat, and truth claim may be sincere, strategic, or mixed; the packet does not force one motive.
The father-son containment parallel and the final garment-as-material-sign model are abductive structural links, not explicit causal explanations supplied by the packet.
The exchange, covert-hearing, and breath-pressure outliers are branch activations and must not be promoted into lexical translations.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **An accusation recruits an older accusation to distribute stigma through kinship.** س ر ق B005, ء خ و B001, and ق ب ل B002 let the brothers explain present suspicion by alleged family precedent. I infer that they transfer blame laterally from Benjamin to Yusuf to protect their own standing.
2. **Concealed inward speech blocks immediate retaliation.** ن ف س B013, ب د و B001 (visible emergence), ش ر ر B001, and و ص ف B001 distinguish hidden judgment from public description. I infer that Yusuf retains his assessment inwardly while exposing only the gap between their position and God’s knowledge.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:89 forced the brothers to revisit what they had done under ignorance, reversing their attempt here to relocate stigma onto Yusuf.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Concealed response as control of disclosure.** `س ر ر:B001` is keeping something hidden inwardly, including a private matter not disclosed. Their accusation links the present brother to an earlier alleged theft; Joseph receives it, conceals the response in himself, and does not make it manifest, while 12:78-80 lets the public negotiation proceed before the brothers withdraw privately. The packet supplies provocation, inner concealment, and continued procedure; I infer that withholding immediate self-disclosure prevents the encounter from collapsing into recognition or retaliation. *Fa-asarrahā ... wa-lam yubdihā* reads as strategic emotional and informational restraint.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:86 has Jacob disclose his grief and sorrow specifically to God, revealing that concealment must be indexed to audience: inward control can prevent reactive speech without requiring absolute silence.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi dalın merkezini erkek ve kadın kardeş ile kardeşlik ilişkisi olarak doğrular. lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın kişi ve ilişki adları ile belirli sözlü yapılar birlikte bulunduğundan, temel kardeşlik anlamı bu yapılara özgü edinme ve karşılıklı bağ kurma anlamlarıyla birleştirilmez.

facets.statement: Temel alan, erkek ve kadın kardeşleri ve aralarındaki doğum ya da soy bağını kapsar.

concept_gloss.applicability: Hem doğumdan gelen kardeşlik bağını hem de bu bağa benzetilerek kardeş sayılan kişileri topluca anlatırken uygundur.

يدخل فيه النفس بمعنى الروح والحياة، وكل إنسان نفس، وخروج النفس عند الموت، والنفس الحية التي بها حياة الجسد.
يدخل فيه النفس بمعنى عين الشيء، ذاته، حقيقته، جملته، كنهه وجوهره، واستعمالها للتوكيد.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyi ayırt edici görünüşü ve nitelikleriyle anlatmayı temel alır; ayrıca şeyin içinde bulunduğu durumu ya da onu tanıtan kalıcı belirtiyi, betimlenebilir oluşu, karşılıklı betimlemeyi ve dil bilgisindeki niteleme görevini kapsar. lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın betimleme ve nitelik çekirdeğini türemiş betimlenme, karşılıklı anlatma ve dilbilgisel niteleme kullanımlarından ayrı tutar.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi ayırt edilmesini sağlayan görünüşü ve nitelikleriyle anlatmak ya da o şeyin içinde bulunduğu, onu tanıtan niteliği belirtmektir. Buna betimlenebilir duruma gelme, bir şeyi karşılıklı olarak betimleme ve dil bilgisinde niteleme görevi de bağlı kullanımlar olarak eklenir.

facets.statement: Bir şeyi görünüşü, durumu ve ayırt edici nitelikleriyle tanıtacak biçimde anlatma.
Bir şeyin içinde bulunduğu durum ya da onu tanıtan kalıcı belirti ve nitelik.
Bir şeyin betimlenmeye elverişli hâle gelmesi veya gözlemcinin gözünde belirli nitelikler kazanması.
Bir şeyi karşılıklı biçimde betimleme ve dil bilgisinde bir varlığı niteleyen ögeyi adlandırma.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Aktarımlar, betimlemeyi bir şeyi tanıtan görünüş ve nitelikleri dile getirme olarak ortaklaştırır. Nitelik, şeyin durumu veya kalıcı belirtisi olarak ele alınır; betimlenebilir olma, karşılıklı betimleme ve dilbilgisel niteleme de bu çekirdeğe bağlıdır.

concept_gloss.text: bir şeyi nitelikleriyle betimleme ve onu belirleyen nitelik
concept_gloss.applicability: Betimleme eylemi ile betimlenen şeyin ayırt edici durumu veya niteliğini birlikte karşılayan genel anlatımdır.

error_profile.preserves: Hem nitelikleri dile getirme eylemini hem de şeyi tanıtan nitelik veya durum boyutunu korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir şeyi görünüşü ve ayırt edici nitelikleriyle anlatan eylem bağlamlarında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Nitelikleri dile getirerek bir şeyi tanıtma eylemini eksiksiz korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir şeyin nasıl olduğunu ya da onu ayırt ettiren kalıcı belirtiyi adlandıran bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Şeyin içinde bulunduğu hâl ile onu tanıtan belirti boyutunu korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir varlığın niteliğini bildiren dilbilgisel ögenin söz konusu olduğu bağlamlara özgüdür.

error_profile.preserves: Dilbilgisel niteleme görevini ve bu görevi taşıyan ögeyi korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, alıcının malı görmediği ve satışın mal için verilen nitelik tarifine dayandığı işlemi açıkça tanımlar; güvence altına alınmış tarifle yapılan biçimi ve işlemin bazı hukuki değerlendirmelerini de bildirir. Verilen dal kimliği bu yapıya sadıktır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnızca nitelik tarifine dayalı görmeden satış yapısına bağlanır ve buradan yalın kök için genel bir satış anlamı çıkarılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir malı önceden görmeye değil, satıcının bildirdiği nitelik tarifine dayanarak satmaktır. Güvence altına alınmış bir tarife bağlanan biçim ile işlemin bağlayıcılığı veya uygun görülmemesi konusundaki aktarımlar bu çekirdeğin özel yönleridir.

facets.statement: Malı görmeden, onun bildirilen nitelik tarifine dayanarak satış yapmak.
Satışı, mal için güvence altına alınmış belirli bir nitelik tarifine bağlamak.
Bu satışın bazı bağlamlarda uygun görülmemesi veya eldeki mal tarif üzere satıldığında bağlayıcı sayılması.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Aktarımlar görmeden yapılan ve malın bildirilen niteliklerine dayanan satışı ortak çekirdek olarak verir. Güvence altına alınmış tarif, işlemin kimi bağlamlarda uygun görülmemesi ve tarif üzere yapılan satışın bağlayıcılığı aynı toplu kanıtta yer alan özel hukuki yönlerdir.
